verses.zh: 「在耶和华―你　神所赐你为业的地上，若遇见被杀的人倒在田野，不知道是谁杀的，
verses.en: If a homicide victim[NOTE:1] should be found lying in a field in the land the Lord your God is giving you,[NOTE:2] and no one knows who killed[NOTE:3] him,
notes: Heb “slain [one].” The term חָלָל (khalal) suggests something other than a natural death (cf. Num 19:16; 23:24; Jer 51:52; Ezek 26:15; 30:24; 31:17-18).
The Hebrew text includes “to possess it,” but this has not been included in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “struck,” but in context a fatal blow is meant; cf. NLT “who committed the murder.”
verses.commentary:
21:1-9 This is a context about how to cleanse the land when a murdered person is found in an open field,
away from any city. Murder pollutes YHWH's land (e.g. Deut. 7:13; 11:9,21; 28:11; 30:20) and must be dealt with in an
appropriate manner (i.e. sacrifice).

verses.zh: 长老和审判官就要出去，从被杀的人那里量起，直量到四围的城邑，
verses.en: your elders and judges must go out and measure how far it is to the cities in the vicinity of the corpse.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “surrounding the slain [one].”
verses.commentary:
21:2 "elders and judges" There are local appointed leaders who sat in the gates of the city and tried the
cases of the community. Only if they had a problem did they take the cases to a higher authority (i.e. Levitical priests,
cf. Deut. 21:5). They measured the distance from the found body to the cities around. The nearest town had to perform
certain rituals (cf. Deut. 21:3-8). This demonstrates their sense of guilt by proximity. The closest city was responsible
for the blood-guiltiness, which could affect YHWH's blessings on the whole region (cf. Deut. 19:13).

verses.zh: 看哪城离被杀的人最近，那城的长老就要从牛群中取一只未曾耕地、未曾负轭的母牛犊，
verses.en: Then the elders of the city nearest to the corpse[NOTE:1] must take from the herd a heifer that has not been worked—that has never pulled with the yoke—
notes: Heb “slain [one].”
verses.commentary:
21:3 "heifer. . .which has not been worked and which has not pulled in a yoke" This means a heifer which has
not been used for agricultural work.

verses.zh: 把母牛犊牵到流水、未曾耕种的山谷去，在谷中打折母牛犊的颈项。
verses.en: and bring the heifer down to a wadi with flowing water,[NOTE:1] to a valley that is neither plowed nor sown.[NOTE:2] There at the wadi they are to break the heifer’s neck.
notes: The combination “a wadi with flowing water” is necessary because a wadi (נַחַל, nakhal) was ordinarily a dry stream or riverbed. For this ritual, however, a perennial stream must be chosen so that there would be fresh, rushing water.
The unworked heifer, fresh stream, and uncultivated valley speak of ritual purity—of freedom from human contamination.
verses.commentary:
21:4 "a valley with running water which has not been plowed or sown" The valley, too, had to be in a natural
state with running water (i.e. not a wadi). The water symbolized carrying the guilt away (similar to the goat of Leviticus 16).

▣ "shall break the heifer's neck" Later rabbinical Midrash said "chopped head off with an ax" because breaking
the neck was a difficult task (cf. Exod. 13:13; 34:20). However, blood does not seem to be involved in the ritual, but
the concept of substitution. The innocent heifer ceremonially takes the place of the unknown murderer. The purpose
was to rid the land of bloodguiltiness (cf. Num. 35:33-34).

verses.zh: 祭司利未的子孙要近前来；因为耶和华―你的　神拣选了他们事奉他，奉耶和华的名祝福，所有争讼殴打的事都要凭他们判断。
verses.en: Then the Levitical priests[NOTE:1] will approach (for the Lord your God has chosen them to serve him and to pronounce blessings in his name,[NOTE:2] and to decide[NOTE:3] every judicial verdict[NOTE:4]) ,
notes: Heb “the priests, the sons of Levi.”
Heb “in the name of the Lord.” See note on Deut 10:8. The pronoun has been used in the translation for stylistic reasons to avoid redundancy.
Heb “by their mouth.”
Heb “every controversy and every blow.”
verses.commentary:
21:5 "the priests" They may refer later to local Levites. In Deuteronomy there is no distinction between priests
and Levites (cf. Deut. 18:1-8).

▣ "to bless in the name of the Lord" Blessing was one of the functions of
priests/Levites (cf. Deut. 10:8; 1 Chr. 23:13). One example of a priestly blessing is recorded in Num. 6:22-26. This blessing
is related to Israel's covenant keeping (cf. Num. 6:27; Deut. 28:3-6). YHWH's personal presence (i.e. name) was honored
or rejected by each Israelite's obedience or willful disobedience to YHWH's revelation (i.e. covenant). Israel's blessing,
both individual (cf. Exod. 19:5-6) and corporate, was determined not by arbitrary or capricious choice, but by personal faith
in YHWH, demonstrated by covenant obedience (lifestyle). YHWH wanted to bless (cf. Exod. 20:24; 2 Chr. 30:27).

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

▣ "every dispute and every assault shall be settled by them" The VERB is the common
one, "to be" (BDB 224, KB 243, Qal IMPERFECT). The translation "be settled" comes from the previous
NOUN phrase, "by their word" (BDB 804).

There are two types of legal problems mentioned:

- "dispute" (i.e. lawsuit) ‒ BDB 936, cf. Deut. 1:12; 19:17; 21:5; 25:1; Exod. 23:2,3,6

- "assault" ‒ BDB 619, cf. Deut. 17:8. Here it refers to physical attack, but the term can mean disease,
cf. Deut. 24:8 (many times in Leviticus).

verses.zh: 那城的众长老，就是离被杀的人最近的，要在那山谷中，在所打折颈项的母牛犊以上洗手，
verses.en: and all the elders of that city nearest the corpse[NOTE:1] must wash their hands over the heifer whose neck was broken in the valley.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “slain [one].”
Heb “wadi,” a seasonal watercourse through a valley.
verses.commentary:
21:6 "wash their hands over the heifer" This symbolizes cleansing (cf. Ps. 26:6; 73:13) from guilt by the
proximity of the dead body. The elders represent the whole community as they corporately wash the guilt away
from the village and area.

verses.zh: 祷告（原文是回答）说：『我们的手未曾流这人的血；我们的眼也未曾看见这事。
verses.en: Then they must proclaim, “Our hands have not spilled this blood, nor have we[NOTE:1] witnessed the crime.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “our eyes.” This is a figure of speech known as synecdoche in which the part (the eyes) is put for the whole (the entire person).
Heb “seen”; the implied object (the crime committed) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
verses.commentary:
21:7 "Our hands did not shed this blood nor did our eyes see it" The rabbinical Midrash relates this to help for the
stranger, poor, orphan, or widow. Since the villagers did not see the stranger's need for help they were absolved
from meeting that need. This may have been a way to stop the victim's family (i.e. blood avenger) from killing an
innocent member of the nearest village in retaliation.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BLOOD AVENGER

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你赦免你所救赎的以色列民，不要使流无辜血的罪归在你的百姓以色列中间。』这样，流血的罪必得赦免。
verses.en: Do not blame[NOTE:1] your people Israel whom you redeemed, O Lord, and do not hold them accountable for the bloodshed of an innocent person.”[NOTE:2] Then atonement will be made for the bloodshed.
notes: Heb “Atone for.”
Heb “and do not place innocent blood in the midst of your people Israel.”
verses.commentary:
21:8

NASB, TEV, NJB
"Forgive"

NKJV
"Provide atonement"

NRSV, JPSOA
"Absolve"

REB
"accept expiation"

LXX
"Be merciful"

Peshitta
"Pardon"

This is the Hebrew VERB "cover" ( BDB 497, KB 493, Piel IMPERATIVE). It is
used twice in this verse (the second use is a Hithpael PERFECT with waw). This term, so common in Leviticus
and Numbers, is used only three times in Deuteronomy: Deut. 21:8 [twice] and Deut. 32:43). Its basic meaning is "to ritually cover by
means of a sacrifice."

SPECIAL TOPIC: ATONEMENT

▣ "redeemed" This VERB (BDB 804, KB 911, Qal PERFECT,
but JUSSIVE in meaning) is parallel to "forgive" (i.e. cover).

SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM

SPECIAL TOPIC: FORGIVENESS IN THE OT

▣

NASB
"do not place the guilt of innocent blood in the

midst of Your people"

NKJV
"do not lay innocent blood to the charge of Your

people"

NRSV, JPSOA
"do not let the guilt of innocent blood remain in

the midst of your people"

TEV
"do not hold us responsible for the murder of an

innocent person"

NJB
"let no innocent blood be shed among your people"

The VERB (BDB 678, KB 733, Qal IMPERFECT, but in
a JUSSIVE sense) is a prayer for ritual absolution from the consequences of an unsolved murder. Notice
how NJB translates the phrase as a JUSSIVE.

verses.zh: 你行耶和华眼中看为正的事，就可以从你们中间除掉流无辜血的罪。」
verses.en: In this manner you will purge the guilt of innocent blood from among you, for you must do what is right before[NOTE:1] the Lord.
notes: Heb “in the eyes of” (so ASV, NASB, NIV).
verses.commentary:
21:9 The ritual (cf. Deut. 21:1-8) was seen as "purging" (BDB 128, KB 145, Piel IMPERFECT) the
effects of corporate sin (i.e. unsolved murders) from the whole community (similar to the rituals of "the Day of Atonement"
in Leviticus 26). Sin, even unintentional corporate sin, affects the blessing of YHWH and even brings collective wrath
(i.e. curses, cf. Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 27-29).

verses.zh: 「你出去与仇敌争战的时候，耶和华―你的　神将他们交在你手中，你就掳了他们去。
verses.en: When you go out to do battle with your enemies and the Lord your God allows you to prevail[NOTE:1] and you take prisoners,
notes: Heb “gives him into your hands.”
verses.commentary:
21:10-14 These verses address how to appropriately deal with women (i.e. not Canaanites, but others,
cf. Deut. 20:10-15) captured in war, even they had rights in YHWH's land. This care for the poor, powerless, and women is
unique in the ancient world's law codes.

verses.zh: 若在被掳的人中见有美貌的女子，恋慕她，要娶她为妻，
verses.en: if you should see among them[NOTE:1] an attractive woman whom you wish to take as a wife,
notes: Heb “the prisoners.” The pronoun has been used in the translation for stylistic reasons, to avoid redundancy.
verses.commentary:
21:11 "woman" This was not a Canaanite woman, a foreigner, but not Canaanite, living in the Promised Land.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WOMEN IN THE BIBLE

▣ Notice the verbal progression:

- "see" ‒ BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal PERFECT with waw

- "love" ‒ BDB 365 I, KB 362, Qal PERFECT with waw, used of YHWH's love
for Israel in Deut. 7:7; 10:15

- "take" ‒ BDB 542, KB 534, Qal PERFECT with waw. Here it does not imply a
sexual union, but a taking into one's house (cf. Deut. 21:12).

This same sequence is found in Gen. 3:6!

verses.zh: 就可以领她到你家里去；她便要剃头发，修指甲，
verses.en: you may bring her back to your house. She must shave her head,[NOTE:1] trim her nails,
notes: This requirement for the woman to shave her head may symbolize the putting away of the old life and customs in preparation for being numbered among the people of the Lord. The same is true for the two following requirements.
verses.commentary:
21:12 "she shall shave her head and trim her nails" This was a

- concluding act (cf. Num. 6:9,18-19)

- cleansing act (cf. Lev. 13:33; 14:8-9)

- mourning act (cf. Deut. 14:1; Lev. 21:5; Jer. 41:5; Ezek. 44:20) ritual

Here it symbolized a new day, a new life, a new family. It is interesting that her conversion to YHWH
is assumed, but not stated. The husband's faith was the family's faith!

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOUSEHOLD BAPTISMS

verses.zh: 脱去被掳时所穿的衣服，住在你家里哀哭父母一个整月，然后可以与她同房。你作她的丈夫，她作你的妻子。
verses.en: discard the clothing she was wearing when captured,[NOTE:1] and stay[NOTE:2] in your house, lamenting for her father and mother for a full month. After that you may sleep with her[NOTE:3] and become her husband and she your wife.
notes: Heb “she is to…remove the clothing of her captivity” (cf. NASB); NRSV “discard her captive’s garb.”
Heb “sit”; KJV, NASB, NRSV “remain.”

The verb בּוֹא (boʾ; “to come”) with the preposition אֶל (ʾel; “to”) means “to approach, to come to” (HALOT 113 s.v. בּוֹא) and is a euphemism for coming together for sexual relations. A clearer euphemism has been used for the translation than the more literal “get together with.” See the note at 2 Sam 12:24 on this phrase being only a euphemism.
verses.commentary:
21:13 "and mourn her father and mother" Although the text does not specifically state that this woman
must be unmarried, it is implied. There is no mention of mourning over the loss of a husband nor the mention of children.

▣ "after that you may go in to her" This is a Hebrew idiom for sexual intercourse (i.e. which consummated
the marriage). Notice that a desire for sexual relations, even with a non-Israelite, is not condemned, but there is an
appropriate time. This month of mourning gives the Hebrew man time to get to know his potential wife. If things do not
go well, there is a way out without divorce.

Also note the apparent absence of an actual marriage ceremony (cf. Gen. 24:67).

verses.zh: 后来你若不喜悦她，就要由她随意出去，决不可为钱卖她，也不可当婢女待她，因为你玷污了她。」
verses.en: If you are not pleased with her, then you must let her go[NOTE:1] where she pleases. You cannot in any case sell[NOTE:2] her;[NOTE:3] you must not take advantage of[NOTE:4] her, since you have already humiliated[NOTE:5] her.
notes: Heb “send her off.” The Hebrew term שִׁלַּחְתָּה (shillakhtah) is a somewhat euphemistic way of referring to divorce, the matter clearly in view here (cf. Deut 22:19, 29; 24:1, 3; Jer 3:1; Mal 2:16). This passage does not have the matter of divorce as its principal objective, so it should not be understood as endorsing divorce generally. It merely makes the point that if grounds for divorce exist (see Deut 24:1-4), and then divorce ensues, the husband could in no way gain profit from it.
The Hebrew text uses the infinitive absolute for emphasis, which the translation indicates by the words “in any case.”
The Hebrew text includes “for money.” This phrase has not been included in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Or perhaps “must not enslave her” (cf. ASV, NAB, NIV, NRSV, NLT); Heb “[must not] be tyrannical over.”

You have humiliated her. Since divorce was considered rejection, the wife subjected to it would “lose face” in addition to the already humiliating event of having become a wife by force (21:11-13). Furthermore, the Hebrew verb translated “humiliated” here (עָנָה, ʿanah), commonly used to speak of rape (cf. Gen 34:2; 2 Sam 13:12, 14, 22, 32; Judg 19:24), likely has sexual overtones as well. The woman may not be enslaved or abused after the divorce because it would be double humiliation (see also E. H. Merrill, Deuteronomy [NAC], 291).
verses.commentary:
21:14 "let her go" This is the technical word for divorce (BDB 1018, KB 1511, Piel PERFECT
with waw). She could not be sold (Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and Qal IMPERFECT of
BDB 569, KB 5181, which was a grammatical way to express emphasis) like a slave, but she could be divorced. See note at Deut. 24:1-4.

means "deal tyrannically with" or "forced to submit to the will of a more powerful person" (cf. Deut. 24:7). YHWH
cares for the fair treatment of even captured women!

intercourse with you"

This VERB (BDB 776, KB 853, Piel PERFECT), in this
context, is best translated like the TEV (e.g. Gen. 34:2; Deut. 22:24,29; Jdg. 19:24; 20:5; 2 Sam. 13:12,14,22,32). These
women would have suffered:

- capture in war

- loss of family

- forced integration into marriage, which also assumes a religious conversion

- now forced removal from the home with no place to go

Notice that this paragraph, and the next also, limits the cultural power of male Israelites!

verses.zh: 「人若有二妻，一为所爱，一为所恶，所爱的、所恶的都给他生了儿子，但长子是所恶之妻生的。
verses.en: Suppose a man has two wives, one whom he loves more than the other,[NOTE:1] and they both[NOTE:2] bear him sons, with the firstborn being the child of the less-loved wife.
notes: Heb “one whom he loves and one whom he hates.” For the idea of שָׂנֵא (saneʾ, “hate”) meaning to be rejected or loved less (cf. NRSV “disliked”), see Gen 29:31, 33; Mal 1:2-3. Cf. A. Konkel, NIDOTTE 3:1256-60.

Heb “both the one whom he loves and the one whom he hates.” On the meaning of the phrase “one whom he loves and one whom he hates” see the note on the word “other” earlier in this verse. The translation has been simplified for stylistic reasons, to avoid redundancy.
verses.commentary:
21:15 This paragraph recognizes the cultural practice of polygamy. The first example in the OT is
Lamech (Gen. 4:23). The most famous early polygamist was Jacob in Genesis 29. Polygamy was practiced in the ANE
among wealthy or powerful people, not usually the common people (although Deut. 21:10-14 could refer to bigamy).

The exact motive for the practice is uncertain:

- sexual

- reproductive (an heir)

- economic

- help poor family

- a way to gain wealth and influence

- a way to handle the spoils of war

- political unions to help neighboring nations maintain peace (i.e. David, Solomon)

▣ "unloved" As verses 10-14 dealt with captured women, verses 15-17 deal with the less favored wife. This
is literally "hated" (BDB 971, cf. Deut. 21:15[twice],16,17). But it is functioning here as a Hebrew idiom of comparison—loved
versus unloved (cf. Gen. 29:30-31; Mal. 1:2-3; Rom. 9:13 [quotes Mal. 1:2-3]; Luke 14:26).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HATE

▣ "firstborn son" The firstborn's rights were established even if he were the son of the unloved wife
(cf. Deut. 21:17; Exod. 13:14-15; Lev. 3:12-13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRSTBORN

verses.zh: 到了把产业分给儿子承受的时候，不可将所爱之妻生的儿子立为长子，在所恶之妻生的儿子以上，
verses.en: In the day he divides his inheritance[NOTE:1] he must not appoint as firstborn the son of the favorite wife in place of the other wife’s[NOTE:2] son who is actually the firstborn.
notes: Heb “when he causes his sons to inherit what is his.”
Heb “the hated.”

verses.zh: 却要认所恶之妻生的儿子为长子，将产业多加一分给他；因这儿子是他力量强壮的时候生的，长子的名分本当归他。」
verses.en: Rather, he must acknowledge the son of the less-loved wife[NOTE:1] as firstborn and give him the double portion[NOTE:2] of all he has, for that son is the beginning of his father’s procreative power[NOTE:3]—to him should go the right of the firstborn.
notes: See note on the word “other” in v. 15.

Heb “measure of two.” The Hebrew expression פִּי שְׁנַיִם (pi shenayim) suggests a two-thirds split; that is, the elder gets two parts and the younger one part. Cf. 2 Kgs 2:9; Zech 13:8. The practice is implicit in Isaac’s blessing of Jacob (Gen 25:31-34) and Jacob’s blessing of Ephraim (Gen 48:8-22).
Heb “his generative power” (אוֹן, ʾon; cf. HALOT 22 s.v.). Cf. NAB “the firstfruits of his manhood”; NRSV “the first issue of his virility.”
verses.commentary:
21:17 "double portion" The Hebrew idiom (BDB 804, "mouth" CONSTRUCT BDB 1040, "double") is also used of
Elisha's desire related to Elijah in 2 Kgs. 2:9. This is the only place in the OT that this double portion is specifically
mentioned. If there were two sons, the older would receive two-thirds and the younger one-third; if three sons,
then 50%, 25%, 25%, etc. The oldest son was to care for the aged parents and administer the family assets.

It is interesting that the historicity of these laws is demonstrated by the archaeological finds of
other ancient law codes:

- Jacob in Genesis 49 gives all his twelve sons equal inheritance. This is reflected in the Code of Hammurabi

- Here the mention of a double share for the firstborn is paralleled in the Nuzi and Mari tablets.

- The differences recorded in Scripture reflect the differences in their contemporary culture (see The Old
Testament Documents by Walter C. Kaiser, Jr., p. 86).

verses.zh: 「人若有顽梗悖逆的儿子，不听从父母的话，他们虽惩治他，他仍不听从，
verses.en: If a person has a stubborn, rebellious son who pays no attention to his father or mother, and they discipline him to no avail,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and he does not listen to them.”
verses.commentary:
21:18-21 This section deals with rebellious sons (i.e. those who did not honor their parents, cf. Deut. 5:16)
and how parents were to treat them (cf. Exod. 21:15,17; Lev. 20:9). Parents did not have the right of life or death over a
child, but the courts did. This concerned

- the violation of Deut. 5:16

- the inheritance within a family

- community solidarity

21:18 This type of antisocial youth was characterized as:

- "stubborn" ‒ BDB 710, KB 770, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE

- "rebellious" ‒ BDB 598, KB 632, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE

- both of these things are used together in Ps. 78:8 and Jer. 5:23

The five PARTICIPLES in this verse show continuous action. The rest of
the verse describes their actions:

- who will not obey parents, Deut. 21:18,20

- he will not even listen to them, Deut. 21:18

- glutton, Deut. 21:20 ‒ BDB 272 II

- drunkard, Deut. 21:20 ‒ BDB 684

See Hard Sayings of the Bible, pp.174-175.

verses.zh: 父母就要抓住他，将他带到本地的城门、本城的长老那里，
verses.en: his father and mother must seize him and bring him to the elders at the gate of his city.
verses.commentary:
21:19 "father and mother shall seize him" This means either

- both parents mutually restrain (BDB 1074, KB 1779, Qal PERFECT with waw)

- the need for two witnesses (cf. Deut. 17:6; 19:15; Num. 35:10)

▣ "at the gateway" The local place of justice was the city gate, where the elders sat (e.g. Deut. 19:12; 22:15; 25:7).

verses.zh: 对长老说：『我们这儿子顽梗悖逆，不听从我们的话，是贪食好酒的人。』
verses.en: They must declare to the elders[NOTE:1] of his city, “Our son is stubborn and rebellious and pays no attention to what we say—he is a glutton and drunkard.”
notes: The LXX and Smr read “to the men,” probably to conform to this phrase in v. 21. However, since judicial cases were the responsibility of the elders in such instances (cf. Deut 19:12; 21:3, 6; 25:7-8) the reading of the MT is likely original and correct here.

verses.zh: 本城的众人就要用石头将他打死。这样，就把那恶从你们中间除掉，以色列众人都要听见害怕。」
verses.en: Then all the men of his city must stone him to death. In this way you will purge[NOTE:1] wickedness from among you, and all Israel[NOTE:2] will hear about it and be afraid.
notes: The Hebrew term בִּעַרְתָּה (biʿartah), here and elsewhere in such contexts (cf. Deut 13:5; 17:7, 12; 19:19; 21:9), suggests God’s anger which consumes like fire (thus בָּעַר, baʿar, “to burn”). See H. Ringgren, TDOT 2:203-4.

Some LXX traditions read הַנִּשְׁאָרִים (hannishʾarim, “those who remain”) for the MT’s יִשְׂרָאֵל (yisraʾel, “Israel”), understandable in light of Deut 19:20. However, the more difficult reading found in the MT is more likely original.
verses.commentary:
21:21 "all the men of his city shall stone him to death" Notice the humanitarian aspect that the parents
did not have to stone their own son. The community (cf. Lev. 20:2,27; 24:14-23; Num. 15:35) acted to rid itself of
evil, willfully recalcitrant members.

Do you still want to take the OT literally in our day?

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE DEATH PENALTY IN ISRAEL

verses.en: his body must not remain all night on the tree; instead you must make certain you bury[NOTE:1] him that same day, for the one who is left exposed[NOTE:2] on a tree is cursed by God.[NOTE:3] You must not defile your land that the Lord your God is giving you as an inheritance.
notes: The Hebrew text uses the infinitive absolute for emphasis, which the translation indicates by “make certain.”
Heb “hung,” but this could convey the wrong image in English (hanging with a rope as a means of execution). Cf. NCV “anyone whose body is displayed on a tree.”

The idea behind the phrase cursed by God seems to be not that the person was impaled because he was cursed but that to leave him exposed there was to invite the curse of God upon the whole land. Why this would be so is not clear, though the rabbinic idea that even a criminal is created in the image of God may give some clue (thus J. H. Tigay, Deuteronomy [JPSTC], 198). Paul cites this text (see Gal 3:13) to make the point that Christ, suspended from a cross, thereby took upon himself the curse associated with such a display of divine wrath and judgment (T. George, Galatians [NAC], 238-39).
verses.commentary:
21:23 "you shall surely bury" This intensified construction combines the INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and
Qal IMPERFECT of "bury" (BDB 868, KB 1064) of the same root. YHWH's wrath demanded the offender's death as
the penalty for his stubborn rebellion. However, YHWH's displeasure would transfer to the community if the body of the
executed covenant violator was not dealt with properly and in a timely fashion.

▣ "(for he who is hanged is accursed of God)" See Gal. 3:13 for Paul's use of this phrase. Paul saw the
substitutionary death of Jesus as taking on Himself the curse of the Mosaic law (i.e. Gal. 3:13; Phil. 2:8). The Mosaic Law became
a death sentence (cf. Ezek. 18:4,20). Originally this curse was related to proper burial procedures in the holy land (i.e. possibly
impaling a corpse on a stake for a brief period of time).

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation
of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above.
Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- Notice the recurrent pattern of "if. . .then." This is one type of ancient Near Eastern law (i.e. case
law or casuistic law), which is distinct from apodictic law (e.g. the Ten Words/Ten Commandments).

SPECIAL TOPIC: LAWS OF THE ANE

- Deuteronomy's law code has several unique features:

- recurrent emphases on covenant love

- YHWH to Israel

- Israelite to Israelite

- Israelite to foreigner

- Israelite to animals

- special care for the poor, disenfranchised, and powerless

- YHWH instructs His people in clear ways (paths). He wants them to understand and
act appropriately. Their actions are to reflect His character as a means of reaching those who do
not yet know Him (personal and national faith relationship). The Law is God's gift to fallen humanity, not
a capricious exercise of control! They show in many practical and specific ways how an "unholy people"
can stay in fellowship with holy God!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE WAY. . .THE PATH
